The Latest Report

The spool is the weapon. A Ukrainian soldier holds a fiber-optic drone and the cable that guides it, immune to jamming. The factories that build them can produce three times what Ukraine’s budget can buy.

Latest Report · Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Paper and Mass

Russia is claiming villages its army has not reached, and Berlin is deciding whether Ukraine’s factories get the money to keep that true. Underneath the paper: a span in the water, a governor’s signature in Belgorod, and a front that went backwards.

This week’s loudest numbers are paper: villages claimed beyond the line, totals announced in Berlin that blur approved, transferred and promised into one figure. The facts with mass are narrower and harder, and they form a chain.

Berlin’s money decides what Ukraine’s factories build. What the factories build decides what the front can hold. The map is the last page of that ledger, not the first.

Read the full report →

Paper and Mass · Evening Report

Four numbers, one argument

Everything was announced. These are the numbers that show what the announcements were worth.

-27.29 sq kmRussia’s net ground change in October
Russian forces seized 139.85 square kilometres and lost 167.14 in October 2026, by the Institute for the Study of War’s count. The claims went the other way.
$32-34BUkraine’s uncommitted 2027 gap
The IMF’s residual financing gap for 2027, before Berlin meets on Thursday. It is the distance between Ukraine’s drone factories idling at a third of capacity and running full.
$44.4BRussia’s liquid savings fund
The National Wealth Fund’s liquid assets on November 1, against a 2027 defence plan of 17.1 trillion roubles, up 27 percent. The cushion is shrinking at both ends of the ledger.
$525MChina’s monthly dual use flow to Russia
Chinese dual use exports to Russia have run at roughly $525 million a month since the invasion. Beijing’s new controls took effect November 18; the shipping data will say whether the valve is closing or being priced.

THE BOARDPURPOSE

Why The Board exists.

I don’t have a ton of time. It’s hard to keep up.

There are so many conflicting narratives, fed by conflicting interests. It feels hard to know what is true, and I know I’m not alone in that.

I often have questions I want answered, or things I don’t understand, that the news simply doesn’t cover. Not all of the time, but sometimes. When that happens, there is nowhere obvious to go for a straight answer.

In my ideal world, I build something useful to me. Something I enjoy reading. Because if I do, so will other people, and it will help them too.

The Board is a personal project. Everything here reflects my own views and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representative of my employer.
